note: Picture-stimulus task, shipped under the 2026-09-05 ruling in references/itemtext_standard.md ('Picture-stimulus tasks: ship the table, leave item_text blank'), following twod_rotation_mather2023. item_text is BLANK by design for all 16 items: expfactory-experiments/stop_signal/experiment.js preloads pentagon.png, hourglass.png, tear.png and square.png and renders each trial as .png>, so the stimuli carry zero characters of readable text and any item_text would be an IRW-authored picture description. The stimulus identity stays where it already is, in the item code. correct_response is BLANK for the reason the ruling itself names: experiment.js assigns the shape-to-key mapping with jsPsych.randomization.shuffle over ['M key','M key','Z key','Z key'], so which of Z/M is correct for a given shape differs by session (confirmed in the raw deposit in batch_029: all 2,088 worker x shape cells have exactly one correct key, while pooled every shape takes both keys at 0.48-0.51). instructions are transcribed verbatim from experiment.js -- the two poldrack-instructions pages plus the post-practice paragraph that introduces the stop signal, which every participant sees before the test phase. The one token that is not verbatim is '[prompt_text]', the source's OWN variable name for the shape-to-key legend at that point in the sentence; the legend is rendered as tags and is participant-specific, so no literal string exists. Nothing else was normalised, expanded or paraphrased. option_text carries the accuracy labels: resp is trial accuracy computed by data/enkavi_2019_conflict_tasks.py::_clean from the source's own boolean 'correct' column, not a chosen response option, so 1='Correct'/0='Incorrect' -- verified cell for cell, see verification sidecar. mapping_basis=data_labels because every item- and resp-specific value shipped comes from the source file's own values with no inference: _prep_stopsignal builds item as condition_SS_trial_type_shape_id from the source's own 'condition' and 'SS_trial_type' columns plus a regex extract of the stimulus PNG stem, and option_text comes from the source's own 'correct' column. A verification row and verify script were written anyway, because the option axis (Correct<->1) is a real claim that route 9 can settle decisively. RIGHTS: not an issue -- the Self-Regulation Ontology deposit is fully open, with the authors' explicit CC BY confirmation recorded in the processing script header; no non-commercial, redistribution or fee clause was found on the task source or the deposit. CARRIED FORWARD from batch_029, unresolved and about the RESPONSE table not the item text: the item code's high/low component is stop-signal FREQUENCY, not delay -- experiment.js draws ss_freq from ['high','low'] and the raw data show 40% stop trials in high blocks vs 20% in low, with SS_delay a separate column, while data/enkavi_2019_conflict_tasks.py maps condition to itemcov_delay. itemcov_ss_frequency would be correct. This affects the shared processing script, not just this table. RETRY TEST: would an unchanged retry, right now, plausibly produce a different result? NO -- this is a clean determinate pass, gated and verified; nothing is outstanding for a retry to resolve.
public_note: The four stimuli in this task are wordless abstract shape images (pentagon, hourglass, tear, square), so item_text is left blank by design and the stimulus identity is carried by the item code instead. There is also no correct_response: the experiment shuffles which of the 'Z' and 'M' keys is correct for each shape separately for every session, so no single key is correct for a shape across respondents. The '[prompt_text]' token in the instructions is the task source's own placeholder for that per-session shape-to-key legend, which was shown to participants as images rather than text. option_text holds scoring labels (Correct/Incorrect) because resp is trial accuracy, not the response option the participant chose.

note: Item wording, response anchors and 0-5 coding all come from Keyes' own MHC-SF description document (PDF authored 'Keyes, Corey', 'MHC-SF Brief Description 12.13.11.doc'), Adult MHC-SF form plus its scoring section. The copy used is the one hosted by the study's own lab, Fredrickson's PEP Lab at UNC (peplab.web.unc.edu/.../MHC-SFoverview.pdf, md5 3f6d411947222e2cc830ba90796a51f6, fetched 2026-09-05); the PLOS article and its S1-S7 supplements do not reproduce any item wording. RIGHTS: that document grants reuse outright -- 'Although copyrighted, the MHC-SF may be used as long as proper credit is given. Permission is not needed to use the measure ... permission is granted here'. No non-commercial clause and no redistribution bar, so nothing in the 2026-09-04/05 rights rulings fires. MAPPING: data/fredrickson_2015_mhcsf.py takes item codes MHCSF_1..MHCSF_14 straight from the S1 xlsx column headers (no positional assignment), and those headers carry no text, so code->wording rests on the canonical numbering; S1 File Table S1 footnote 2 states 'Items are ordered as in ... the MHC-SF instrument' and its item-factor allocation (h=1-3, s=4-8, p=9-14) matches Keyes' canonical clusters exactly. Verified numerically -- see verification_fredrickson_2015_mhcsf.csv. DEVIATIONS from literal transcription, all deliberate: (a) the form's leading item numbers and a layout artifact ('SEE BELOW' printed before item 6) were stripped; (b) the six anchors are printed in the response grid in full caps (NEVER, ONCE OR TWICE, ...) and are shipped in the sentence case used by the same document's scoring syntax, which is also where the 0-5 coding is stated verbatim ('never=0, once or twice=1, about once a week=2, about 2 or 3 times a week=3, almost every day=4, every day=5'); (c) the instrument's own grammatical slip ('the following questions are about') is preserved verbatim; (d) the trailing ellipsis character was written as three ASCII dots. Item 6 is shipped in the document's current wording; the same document notes the original wording was 'that our society is becoming a better place for people like you' and the study does not say which it used. Response direction corroborated by content: MHCSF_6 (society becoming a better place) has the lowest mean, 1.63, and MHCSF_2 ('interested in life') the highest, 3.87, which is only coherent if 0=Never..5=Every day.
public_note: Item wording is the canonical Keyes MHC-SF (the study reproduces none); two caveats follow from that. The shipped instructions are the paper form's, including 'Place a check mark in the box', while this study administered the questionnaire online, and item 6 is given in the current wording ('that our society is a good place, or is becoming a better place, for all people') although Keyes sanctions an alternative original wording and the study does not state which version its participants saw.
